label: Flooring

steps.what: Lay rows in order; each row's cut pieces are labelled row and end.

benefits.value: 0.9% with offcut carry vs about 10% typical allowance
benefits.detail: 230 planks of 1829 x 190 for 79.2 m2 in rooms 101 and 201; offcuts of 300 mm or more reused as row starters or end pieces; last-row rip not counted. Room 201 is a rectangle of the model area (est.).

FMI puts rework at about 5% of construction spend and 48% of rework on poor communication or data. If labelled, sequenced, pre-checked parts prevent 15 to 30% of this trade's rework (estimate), callbacks fall by 0.75 to 1.50% of trade spend.

cell_does: Cuts 97 plank starter/end pieces in row order; 45 rows start with the previous row's offcut.
Cuts thresholds and stair nosings to length.
cell_cannot: Rip the last row to width (crosscut only).
app: Takeoff: boxes of flooring per room; row list.
code: Manufacturer installation (expansion gap 12 mm, end-joint stagger >= 300 mm); BCBC 9.30 flooring
summary: Plank rows laid out per room: the cell cuts every starter and end piece, carries each offcut to start the next row, and keeps end joints 300 mm apart.
highlight: Row-by-row plank layout: 45 rows start from an earlier offcut, 0.9% crosscut waste (last-row rip excluded) on 230 planks.
routing: Acucut routing: the cell's nester groups this trade's parts by section and stock length, cuts them in bundle order (last-installed at the bottom), laser-burns the label, QR and every mark listed, and drops each bundle in its zone so the crew picks in install order.
